title: Probabilistic Cache-Tier Economic Scenarios (Nov 2025)
summary: Working workbook that models a 3-tier cache (hot / prefetch / long-tail KV) with probabilistic hit-rate distributions. Calculates expected per-request and per-million-token savings across workload mixes and sequence-length profiles; includes stochastic scenario sampling and quick sensitivity heatmaps for product recommendations.
key_assumptions: Three cache tiers: hot (immediate), prefetch (short-lived prefix), long-tail KV (persistent small-value vectors)
Unit compute cost: $0.0012 per token served from model A (full precision host), $0.00035 per token for quantized fallback model B
KV serving marginal cost: $0.00002 per token for hit response (memory/IO amortized), additional $0.00015 per miss due to backend model call
Average request token lengths modeled as distribution buckets: short (<=40), medium (41-200), long (>200)
Workload composition is parameterized by percent queries with prefix reuse vs one-off prompts
Cache eviction dynamics summarized by TTLs: hot=30s, prefetch=60s, long-tail=7 days (configurable)
Throughput SLO requires p95 latency < 250ms; high batching (>=8) allowed only for non-interactive paths
methodology: We sample 10k synthetic request traces per scenario using configurable distributions for sequence length, prefix-reuse probability, and inter-arrival time. For each trace the cache decision engine probabilistically assigns hits to tiers based on TTL and reuse; cost per request = cost_from_cache_hit + cost_of_miss_path (including quantized fallback where configured). Aggregated metrics compute expected savings relative to baseline no-cache and baseline single-tier cache. Monte Carlo percentiles reported (5th, 50th, 95th).
tabs:
Inputs - scenario parameters as key/value table: (baseline token cost, fallback model cost, kv-cost-per-hit, ttl-hot, ttl-prefetch, ttl-longtail, hit-lambda per tier, request-rate)
user can edit distribution params and see immediate results.
Distribution-Sampler - sample counts by bucket: headers: bucket, prob, avg_tokens, sample_count. Example rows: short,0.55,28,5500; medium,0.35,120,3500; long,0.10,420,1000.

Cache-Model - probabilistic routing logic and derived per-request state columns: timestamp, seq_len, prefix_id, tier_hit (hot|prefetch|longtail|miss), model_path (A|B|cached), cost_usd, latency_ms. (sheet contains formulas, not raw code)

Scenario-Results - summary rows per scenario: scenario_name, p_hit_total, p_hit_hot, p_hit_prefetch, p_hit_longtail, avg_cost_per_request_usd, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, pct_savings_vs_no_cache, pct_savings_vs_single_tier_cache, p95_latency_ms
Sensitivity-Heatmap - grid of percent_savings vs hit_rate_prefetch (x-axis) and seq_length_mix (y-axis) exported as CSV-like matrix for quick visual import into Slides
Recommendations - human-readable output block with suggested cache TTLs, prefetch window, and fallback quantization levels for this workload mix
sample_formulae: avg_cost_cached = p_hot/p_hit_total * cost_hot + p_prefetch/p_hit_total * cost_prefetch + p_longtail/p_hit_total * cost_longtail
cost_per_1M_tokens = expected_cost_per_request * requests_per_1M_tokens (scaled by avg token count)
scenario_highlights: Interactive chat-heavy workload (65% short queries, high prefix reuse): model suggests increasing hot-tier TTL to 45s and boosting prefetch parallelism -> median savings ~31% vs no-cache, 12% vs single-tier cache

Batch embedding-style workload (30% long queries, low prefix reuse): long-tail KV pays off only if longtail hit > 6% and kv read latency <15ms; otherwise quantized fallback model reduces cost more reliably
Microburst traffic with high arrival variance: auto-scaling cold-starts erode savings unless prefetch window extended; recommended conservative prefetch window for low-SLA customers
Edge-case: extremely high seq-length tail (>5% >2000 tokens) increases cost variability; provide contract for dedicated capacity or adjust routing to quantized model for long sequences
notes_and_next_steps: Share with SEs for two customer pilots (fintech chat and marketing content generation) - ask SEs to provide real prefix_reuse traces
Instrument lightweight sampler in hosted API to export prefix_reuse histogram for 7 days
Validate KV read latencies under 95th percentile load before recommending long-tail enablement
Follow-up: convert heatmap into 2 annotated slides for the Nov 17 product review
Status: draft - needs validation from SRE on kv cost numbers and from applied-ml on fallback quality tradeoffs
